question: Does the old module-18 probe correctly treat the lifecycle receiver as a full cLuxUserModule with a script owner at +0x90 and an OnAction discriminator at RVA 0x1378e0?
claim: No. Constructor and RTTI-backed vtables prove that lifecycle receives full module +0x110. The full object itself owns script-wrapper fields, including low script object +0xe8 and context manager +0x10. RVA 0x1378e0 belongs to cLuxMapHandler. PostUpdate RVA 0x1ab3a0 adjusts back to the full owner before preparing/executing script. This corrects a silent discovery failure; it does not prove runtime acceptance of the new bootstrap.
method: Ghidra MCP against explicitly selected /SOMA/Soma_NoSteam.exe: constructor and PostUpdate disassembly/decompilation, raw vtables and RTTI, method cache and context callees. Independently read installed PE with scripts/Test-HandsBootstrapContract.ps1: six source signatures exact and unique, five concrete virtual callees checked. Initial 31-byte PostUpdate prefix had five matches; final 57-byte contract is unique. No game launch. Ghidra labels/comments corrected and program saved.

identity.reason: Installed NoSteam SHA256 recorded and checked by offline PE script; selected Ghidra program is x64 at image base 0x140000000. Raw tables agree with the file.

instrument.reason: Ghidra raw bytes/constructor output corroborated by separate offline PE signature and virtual-callee checks. Read-only endpoints used; no debugger or game execution.

control.reason: Full/secondary constructor stores and PostUpdate receiver adjustment independently agree. RTTI traces the alleged OnAction owner to cLuxMapHandler. A nonunique prefix failed the checker before strengthening, demonstrating rejection coverage.

scene.reason: Static binary ownership investigation; no scene or live process required.

restore.reason: No game/runtime mutation. Source changes and Ghidra annotations are persistent development artifacts, separate from this static receiver verdict.

baseline.reason: No game launch or headset run. Eleven automated tests pass for the implementation, but that is not gameplay baseline health.

limits: Only the named executable and inspected installed script contracts. Before-vial creation, authored animation coexistence, campaign hand-model changes and headset appearance remain pending. Dispatch success is not native-seed or headset acceptance. The old inventory observer's owner assumption is also suspect and is documented for separate review, not claimed fixed.

artifacts.role: Raw Ghidra constructor, method, vtable and RTTI evidence
Interpretation, ABI, lifecycle gates and runtime limitations

do_not_repeat.approach: Identify a native script module from a matching registered method name and read full-object offsets relative to its secondary lifecycle receiver.
do_not_repeat.reason: The same declaration is implemented by multiple native owners; this target's secondary base is +0x110 and the alleged OnAction belongs to cLuxMapHandler.
do_not_repeat.reopen_when: A different executable has constructor/RTTI/callee proof of a different receiver layout.

next_action: Fleet candidate: strengthen receiver/subobject and registration-versus-native-owner guidance. Next authorized headset test must confirm pre-vial native seed, compatible authored animations, reload and exit; do not mark always-visible campaign arms accepted from static evidence.
